claims.statement: Open-Inspect state splits across two SQLite databases: shared D1 (`env.DB`) holds the cross-session system of record (sessions index, environments, automations, image builds, secrets, skills, users, model-provider accounts), while each Session Durable Object owns an embedded SQLite database holding hot session state (participants, messages, events, artifacts, sandbox, per-repo git state); D1 is accessed via the async `SqlDatabase` port and the DO's `SqlStorage` is a deliberately separate synchronous engine.

`SqlDatabase` (`src/db/sql-database.ts`) is the engine-neutral port all shared-state stores are built on: `D1Database` satisfies it structurally (compile-time asserted, no runtime wrapper), `batch()` must execute as a single atomic transaction with positional results, and `meta.changes` is a required field that store call sites (CAS conflict detection, guarded transitions, insert-vs-update detection) gate correctness on.

D1 SQL access is organized as per-aggregate stores in `src/db/` (SessionIndexStore, EnvironmentStore, AutomationStore, ImageBuildStore, SkillStore, UserStore, the secrets stores, etc.), each taking a `SqlDatabase`, keeping snake_case rows in the database and camelCase types at the API boundary; the router injects `instrumentD1(env.DB, metrics)`, a transparent wrapper that records per-query timing and rows read/written into the request's wide event.

D1 migrations live in `terraform/d1/migrations/` as `NNNN_description.sql` files (numeric prefix = tracked version) and are applied by `scripts/d1-migrate.sh <database-name>`: it fails fast on prefix-less filenames and duplicate prefixes, maintains a `_schema_migrations (version, name, applied_at)` ledger, rejects a version recorded under a different filename, and submits each pending migration plus its ledger INSERT as one `wrangler d1 execute --remote --file` call so a failed migration rolls back and a lost response is safely retryable.

Terraform drives migration application: `terraform/environments/production/d1.tf` declares a `null_resource` whose trigger is the sha256 over the sorted migration file set, so `terraform apply` re-runs `d1-migrate.sh` whenever any migration file changes, and the D1 database is created with read replication disabled.

Control-plane integration tests apply the real D1 migrations automatically: `vitest.integration.config.ts` loads `terraform/d1/migrations` with `readD1Migrations()` into a `TEST_MIGRATIONS` binding, and the setup file `test/integration/apply-migrations.ts` calls `applyD1Migrations(env.DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS)` before any test runs — so a new table needs both a migration file and store updates, because store-only changes pass typecheck but fail at runtime against the migrated D1.

D1 migration backfills are written guarded (`NOT EXISTS` / `IS NULL`) so re-running them is the idempotent roll-forward repair path, while schema-changing statements (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) in the same file are applied exactly once via `_schema_migrations` because SQLite has no ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS.

Migrations 0039/0040 replaced the per-kind `repo_images`/`environment_images` tables with the unified `image_builds` registry, copying environment rows verbatim (they already carried fingerprints) and dropping the old tables; the control-plane scheduler naturally rebuilds enabled scopes so no legacy backfill job was required.

The per-session DO schema uses a two-path design: `SCHEMA_SQL` gives fresh DOs the complete current schema, while `MIGRATIONS` is an ordered numbered list tracked in a DO-local `_schema_migrations (id, applied_at)` table applied to existing DOs; `initSchema(sql)` = SCHEMA_SQL, then applyMigrations, then indexes, and `SessionDO.ensureInitialized()` calls it on every activation (first touch after construction or eviction) before building the runtime graph.

The fresh-DO and migrated-DO schema paths are kept from diverging by shared SQL constants — e.g. `SESSION_REPOSITORIES_TABLE_SQL` is used both inside `SCHEMA_SQL` and as migration 31 — and a unit test asserts both paths create the table; `runMigration` swallows only duplicate-column/already-exists errors and rethrows everything else, and function-type migrations must be idempotent because a crash between execution and recording can re-run them.

`sessions` (migration 0002) is the queryable session index, one row per session with title, the scalar primary-repository mirror (`repo_owner`/`repo_name`/`base_branch`), model, status, lineage (`parent_session_id`, `spawn_source`, `spawn_depth`, and `root_session_id` added in 0063 with a cycle-safe recursive backfill), automation linkage (`automation_id`, `automation_run_id`), launch provenance (`environment_id`), analytics mirrors (`scm_login`, `user_id`, `total_cost`, `active_duration_ms`, `message_count`, `pr_count`), and the all-or-none `latest_terminal_message_*` triple added in 0055.

`session_repositories` (0032) holds a session's ordered member repositories — `position` 0 is the primary, mirrored into the scalar session row columns — with `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `sessions`; pre-feature sessions have no rows and readers synthesize a one-entry list from the scalar columns.

The row-0-mirrors-scalars invariant is enforced at session creation: `initializeSession` throws when `repositories[0]` does not match the scalar repository fields, and the DO `session_repositories` table comment documents that position 0 mirrors into `session.repo_owner`/`repo_name`.

`SessionIndexStore.create()` validates repo fields together (lowercased/trimmed, blank pairs nulled), requires the `providerAuth` snapshot to be complete across every subscription provider, and writes the session row, `session_repositories` rows, pinned skill manifest, and provider-auth rows in one atomic `db.batch`; a skipped insert (0 changes) throws because `initialize.ts` relies on D1 failures being caught before any sandbox spawns — and D1 is written first, before DO initialization.

`SessionIndexStore.updateStatus` only applies monotonic `updated_at` values (`AND updated_at <= ?`) to protect the index from out-of-order async writes, while `repairStatus` and `archiveOrphanedDraft` are deliberately unguarded repair paths used by the abandoned-draft sweep to fix a drifted draft projection without claiming new activity.

`acquireChildAdmissionLease` claims parent concurrency capacity in the `child_admission_leases` table (0058) with a 5-minute TTL, counting live children plus unexpired leases against `maxConcurrentChildren` in a single guarded statement; leases are released by token on completion or expiry.

The D1 sessions index is the WebSocket routing authority: the worker's upgrade path answers 404 for a session id absent from `sessions` (`SessionIndexStore.exists`) before any Durable Object is resolved.

`session_pull_requests` (0041) makes D1 the queryable authority record for PRs created by sessions — the DO `pr` artifact is a live-view mirror — keyed by the DO artifact id, with a `lifecycle_state IN ('open','closed','merged')` CHECK, a draft-only-while-open invariant, a monotonic `provider_updated_at` guard on upserts, and canonical identity `(repository_external_id, pr_number)` with a legacy `(repo_owner, repo_name, pr_number)` fallback.
`session_read_states` (0055) stores per-user last-read message per session, cascading from both `users` and `sessions`, serving the unread projections on session lists.

`repo_metadata` (0002) is the repository catalog with description, aliases, and Slack channel associations, extended by `image_build_enabled` (0010, the per-repo prebuild toggle) and `default_environment_id` (0036, the GitHub-bot workspace redirect).

`environments` (0033) is a named, prebuildable repository set: `environment_repositories` stores the ordered members with per-repository `base_branch`, the name is unique case-insensitively (the stable `env_<id>` is what Slack/Linear targets reference), and `environment_secrets` mirrors `repo_secrets` with the same encryption key and caps.

The environment delete cascade is deliberate: `environment_repositories` and `environment_secrets` are owned children with `ON DELETE CASCADE`; `image_builds` rows are superseded (not cascaded, FK-less on purpose) so the cleanup reaper can still reclaim provider artifacts; `sessions.environment_id` is FK-less so sessions keep a benignly dangling provenance id — and `EnvironmentStore.delete` composes repository deletion, secret deletion, build supersession, and the environment delete into one atomic `db.batch`.

Secrets have three D1 scopes sharing one store plumbing: `global_secrets` (0004), `repo_secrets` (0001, keyed by `(repo_id, key)`), and `environment_secrets` (0033); all three encrypt with `REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and go through `src/db/scoped-secrets.ts`, which owns only the scope-independent pieces while each store keeps its own table-specific SQL and API.

`image_builds` (0039, extended by 0052) is the unified prebuilt-image registry for both scope kinds — `scope_kind` is `repo` (scope_id = lowercase owner/name) or `environment` (scope_id = environment id) — carrying the provider artifact id, per-repository SHAs (`repository_shas` JSON `[{repoOwner, repoName, baseSha}]`), the `repositories_fingerprint` for spawn matching, the `runtime_version` (SANDBOX_VERSION at build time), status `building|ready|failed|superseded`, callback-token state (hash only, expiry, used_at), Queue-finalization lease state (`completion_hash`, `finalization_lease_token/expires_at`), and `provider_session_cleanup_pending`.

`ImageBuildStore.registerBuild` is the authoritative concurrency-1 gate for image builds: a single `INSERT … SELECT … WHERE NOT EXISTS (a building row for the same scope+provider)` is atomic within one statement so concurrent triggers cannot both insert; `bindProviderSession` then binds the provider session and sets `provider_session_cleanup_pending = 1`.

Image-build callback acceptance is a conditional UPDATE requiring the exact bound `provider_session_id`, a hash-compared, unexpired, single-use callback token, and `status = 'building'`; an exact duplicate is reported as a replay (safe republish after a lost HTTP response, since accepted callbacks stay authorizable) and any conflicting or stale callback is rejected without changing the row.

Image-build finalization happens off the request path: callbacks atomically accept the payload in D1 then publish a secret-free command to Cloudflare Queue, whose consumer claims an exclusive lease (expired leases replaceable), transitions the row to `ready`/`superseded`/`failed`, and performs idempotent provider-session cleanup; sweep SQL constants (`MARK_STALE_IMAGE_BUILDS_SQL`, `PROVIDER_SESSION_CLEANUP_SQL`, `SUPERSEDED_IMAGES_SQL`, `FAILED_IMAGE_ARTIFACTS_SQL`) reap stale/failed/superseded rows, with matching partial indexes added in migration 0053.

At spawn time a session boots from its scope's ready prebuilt image only if the image's `repositories_fingerprint` equals the fingerprint of the session's own repository snapshot (not the scope's current repositories) and its `runtime_version` passes `MIN_COMPATIBLE_RUNTIME_VERSION` (the floor fails closed on an unparseable version); any miss falls back to the base image — sessions are never blocked on builds.

`automations` (0013, reshaped by 0029/0031) holds trigger configuration — `trigger_type`, `schedule_cron`/`schedule_tz`, `event_type`, JSON `trigger_config`, encrypted `trigger_auth_data` — plus model/instructions, `enabled`, `next_run_at`, `consecutive_failures`, and soft delete (`deleted_at`); the scalar repository columns were dropped in 0031, so the live target selection lives only in the normalized tables.

`automation_repositories` (0030) and `automation_environments` (0037) are the live target selection, unique per `(automation_id, repo_owner, repo_name)` and per `(automation_id, environment_id)`; zero rows is a repo-less automation — behavior derives from the data, with no mode enum or JSON blob.

`automation_invocations` (0030) is one thin row per firing: `source` (`schedule`|`manual`|`event`, distinct from the configured trigger type), `scheduled_at` (the cron slot, CHECK-required for schedule sources), the firing-scoped `trigger_key` (event dedup via `UNIQUE (automation_id, trigger_key) WHERE trigger_key IS NOT NULL`), `concurrency_key` (per-key overlap scope), `trigger_metadata`, `skip_reason` (present iff a skipped childless firing), and `failure_counted_at`; a partial unique index on `(automation_id, scheduled_at)` for schedule sources dedups cron double-fires, and status is never stored on the invocation.

`automation_runs` is the per-target, session-linked unit — one row per repository or environment per invocation, required by 0059 to have `NOT NULL invocation_id` (a table-rebuild migration that aborts on malformed rows rather than inventing data) — and each run snapshots its target at firing time (`repo_owner/repo_name/repo_id/base_branch` or `environment_id`), making history self-contained so editing the live selection never rewrites the past; unique indexes enforce at most one run per repository and per environment per invocation.

Invocation status is derived, never stored: `DERIVED_INVOCATION_STATUS_SQL` in `automation-store.ts` is the single SQL definition aggregated over child runs (no children → skipped; any active child → starting until one leaves starting, then running; all terminal → completed/failed/partial_failed/skipped), mirrored by a TypeScript twin `deriveInvocationStatus` that integration tests keep in lockstep — deriving removes the crash-between-last-child-and-parent-update wedge class.

`AutomationStore.insertInvocationGuarded` creates the invocation, its child runs, and the schedule advance in one D1 batch where every statement is self-guarded: the invocation insert is suppressed when an overlap predicate matches (automation-wide for schedule/manual, per `concurrency_key` for events), child inserts are no-ops when the invocation was suppressed, and the schedule advance is a compare-and-set on the claimed cron slot (`WHERE next_run_at = ?`, deliberately not a monotonic-timestamp guard which would let a loser skip a slot); a UNIQUE violation (cron double-fire, event dedup) rolls back the whole batch and callers classify it via `isDuplicateKeyError`.

`tryMarkInvocationFailureCounted` is a compare-and-set on `automation_invocations.failure_counted_at` (`WHERE failure_counted_at IS NULL`) so exactly one racing callback counts an invocation's failure toward auto-pause; a recovery sweep finds recent all-terminal invocations with a failed child whose failure was never counted (the crash-after-last-callback window).

`automation_slack_channels` (0026) is the watched-channel join table for slack_event automations, letting channel-keyed event selection find candidate automations by channel index instead of scanning and JSON-parsing every automation's trigger_config.

The skills subsystem (0061, `src/db/skills.ts`) separates the mutable catalog row (`skills`: enabled flag, soft delete, `current_revision_id`) from immutable content in `skill_revisions` (`UNIQUE (skill_id, revision_number)`, content sha256, body, metadata) with files in `skill_revision_files`; database triggers abort any `current_revision_id` that does not belong to the skill.

`skill_assignments` grants applicability with exactly one of global/repository/environment scope shapes (CHECK-enforced); assignment writes — and environment renames affecting provenance — advance the `skills_catalog_state` singleton `generation` that session skill resolution uses to retry consistent snapshots; `skill_profiles`/`skill_profile_items` are per-user named filters that do NOT grant applicability (resolution intersects profile ids with assigned enabled skills) and their writes also bump the generation.

`session_skill_manifests` + `session_skill_revisions` pin the immutable resolved skill set per session (selection mode, resolver version, manifest sha256, per-revision provenance); the manifest is written atomically inside the session-creation batch (`SessionIndexStore.create`) or copied verbatim from the parent session for agent-spawned children, so a session cannot exist without a consistent pinned manifest.

`skill_import_sources` (0069) records per-revision import provenance for repository-imported skills (provider, repo, resolved ref, commit sha pinning a moving ref to immutable bytes, and a source_sha256 distinct from the regenerated revision digest); editor-authored revisions have no row, so a skill's recorded source is its most recent import and survives later hand edits.

Integration settings resolve through three layers, lowest precedence first: `integration_settings` (0007, global defaults by `integration_id`), `integration_repo_settings` (0007, per-repo overrides), and `integration_environment_settings` (0038, the top layer keyed by `(integration_id, environment_id)`, `ON DELETE CASCADE` from environments); only the session-scoped integrations (`sandbox`, `code-server`) accept the environment level, enforced by the store's `supportsEnvironmentSettings` allowlist.

`users` + `user_identities` (0019, `src/db/user-store.ts`) is the canonical user model: one canonical record per person with free-form `provider` identity links unique per `(provider, provider_user_id)` — no CHECK constraint, so new auth/SCM providers need no migration; `sessions`, `automations`, and `user_scm_tokens` all carry a nullable `user_id` for attribution.

Better Auth is configured so its user model IS the canonical `users` table and its account model IS `user_identities` (with the OAuth credential columns `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`id_token` added there in migration 0057), with `encryptOAuthTokens: true` so credential columns are written as ciphertext; `auth_sessions` keeps browser sessions and `auth_verifications` OAuth state.
`verified_email_claims` and `browser_auth_sessions` (0047) hold mailbox-ownership proofs and browser session tokens (hash-at-rest) with absolute-expiry and revocation CHECK constraints.

`api_tokens` (0044) are control-plane-issued opaque credentials (web_session and web_session_refresh kinds) — hash-at-rest with a rotation `family_id`, `rotated_to` successor pointer, family expiry cap copied through rotation, and a plain `expires_at` index for the retention sweep.

Subscription-provider account storage (0064/0065): `model_provider_accounts` (status `active`/`disabled`/`reconnect_required`, unique external identity per provider among non-archived rows, `lifecycle_version` for optimistic concurrency), `model_provider_account_credentials` (encrypted payload, versioned schema, and a strict `exchange_state` machine — `idle` xor `in_flight` with owner and started-at, CHECK-enforced — fencing token exchanges), `model_provider_account_defaults` (one default per provider, with a trigger refusing to disable/archive the default account), `session_model_provider_auth` (per-session immutable auth snapshot with CHECK-constrained modes), and `model_provider_account_authorizations` (the heavily CHECK-constrained device-flow state machine).

`D1ModelProviderAccountAtomicWriter` composes the account, credential, authorization, and default stores so account + credential + default are written in one `db.batch` on creation, and reconnects verify both the expected credential version and account state in the same batch — a failed exchange can never leave a half-connected account.

Other encrypted D1 tables use `REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`: `mcp_servers` (0018, revision added in 0062) encrypts env/header values (empty maps stored as plaintext `{}` sentinel), and `commit_signing_configuration` (0043) stores the commit-signing private key encrypted in a singleton row.

`pr_autofix_feedback` (0070) is the durable receipt/decision ledger for PR feedback Autofix — recording why a provider object was or was not dispatched (decision `received`/`queued`/`skipped`/`failed`) — while execution admission stays authoritative in the owning Session Durable Object.

The DO `session` table holds hot core state: external name, title, scalar primary repo mirror, per-session model/reasoning default, status (`created`/`active`/`completed`/`failed`/`archived`/`cancelled`), lineage (`parent_session_id`, `spawn_source`, `spawn_depth`), `code_server_enabled`/`vnc_enabled`, `total_cost`, resolved `sandbox_settings` JSON, `environment_id` provenance, and `opencode_session_id`; a CHECK requires `repo_owner`/`repo_name` to be null together and no-repo sessions to lack branch context.

The DO `participants` table stores session members with SCM identity for git commit attribution, AES-GCM-encrypted `scm_access_token_encrypted`/`scm_refresh_token_encrypted`, and `ws_auth_token` stored as a SHA-256 hash (never plaintext) for WebSocket authentication.

The DO `messages` table is the prompt queue and history with status `pending`/`processing`/`completed`/`failed`, per-message model/reasoning overrides, Slack callback context, web idempotency (`client_request_id` unique partial index), Autofix dedup keys, and `stop_confirmation_deadline`; a unique partial index enforces at most one `processing` message per session (migration 42 repaired duplicates by requeueing later claims).

The DO `events` table is the append-only agent event log (tool calls, tool results, tokens, errors) with a `UNIQUE timeline_sequence` (added in migration 38, backfilled from rowid) for stable ordering and cursor-based pagination.

The DO `sandbox` table holds the selected backend sandbox: provider/snapshot ids, `runtime_version` and `snapshot_runtime_version` (restore compatibility floor), sandbox auth token (hash preferred), the status machine (`pending`→`spawning`→`connecting`→`warming`→`ready` plus `stale`/`snapshotting`/`stopped`/`failed`), `git_sync_status`, heartbeats, a spawn-failure circuit breaker (`spawn_failure_count`), and rotating code-server/VNC/tunnel URLs and passwords; `session_diff` is a singleton holding the latest durable checkout diff bundle (the only home of source patches), and `session_alarm_state` persists alarm scheduling state for DO adoption recovery.

The DO's `session_repositories` table extends the D1 identity subset with per-repo git state (`branch_name`, `base_sha`, `current_sha`) — git state is DO-only and deliberately absent from the D1 index ("D1 doesn't store it"), with pre-feature readers overlaying the position-0 row with the session scalar columns.
The DO `ws_client_mapping` table maps WebSocket ids to participants so connections recovered from WebSocket hibernation can be re-authenticated after DO eviction.

The DO is the live authority and D1 a projection of selected facts: `SessionStatusService` is the single place every status transition fans out — connected clients (broadcast), the D1 session index (status plus terminal metrics via `updateMetrics`), and the parent session's Durable Object (child rollup) — with D1 writes monotonicity-guarded; projection failures are caught and logged, and `repairIndexStatus` re-projects without claiming new activity.

`TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is the AES-256-GCM key domain (`encryptToken`/`decryptToken` in `src/auth/crypto.ts`: 256-bit key, 96-bit random IV, base64-encoded `IV || ciphertext`) protecting SCM enrichment tokens — participant tokens in the DO `participants` table and the D1 `user_scm_tokens` refresh-token store; rotating it invalidates stored SCM tokens and affected users re-link.

`UserScmTokenStore.upsertTokens` only overwrites when the incoming token expires later (`WHERE excluded.token_expires_at > ...`), and `casUpdateTokens` performs a refresh-token compare-and-set on the raw ciphertext so concurrent refreshes cannot clobber each other.

`REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is the single key for all three secret scopes and also for other stored control-plane secrets: automation `trigger_auth_data` (e.g. Sentry client secrets via `encryptSentrySecret`), MCP server env/header values, and the commit-signing private key; `src/db/scoped-secrets.ts` provides the shared write validation, per-scope key cap, encryption bookkeeping, and row codecs, with `SecretDecryptionError` carrying the failing key but never plaintext or ciphertext.

`src/db/secrets-validation.ts` enforces the rules gating every secret write: keys must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` (max 256 chars) and not be in the reserved-key blocklist (system env vars like `SANDBOX_AUTH_TOKEN`, `PATH`, `GITHUB_APP_TOKEN`), values max 16 KB, max 50 keys and 64 KB total per scope; `mergeSecretSources` folds ordered per-session sources lowest-precedence-first (the primary repository passed last so it wins collisions) with per-source byte attribution and a 128 KiB combined session cap.

`PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (implemented in `src/auth/provider-account-crypto.ts`) encrypts subscription-provider credentials with a versioned envelope (`v1.<iv>.<ciphertext>`) and AES-GCM additional authenticated data binding the provider account id, provider, and credential schema version — a ciphertext cannot be decrypted under a different account context; rotation requires an explicit migration that re-encrypts every credential while both keys are available.

Encryption keys are validated fail-closed at startup (`src/env-validation.ts`): each key must be present, strict base64, and decode to exactly 32 bytes for AES-256, so a malformed key fails at first touch rather than mid-spawn and a short key cannot silently downgrade to AES-128/192.
